statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-46597 (GO-2026-5013, GHSA-q4h4-gmj2-qvw2): byte arithmetic in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh can underflow and panic, fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5013, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q4h4-gmj2-qvw2). Inspected every published build of the alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 through 0.35.0-r2 (there is no 0.33.1-r4), on both x86_64 and aarch64, 72 packages, each verified against the repository index checksum. The payload of every package is two files, usr/bin/alertmanager and usr/bin/amtool: statically linked Go programs (no ELF interpreter) built for GOOS=linux with CGO_ENABLED=0. The function names the Go linker records in each binary (its function-name table) were searched, leaving out the standard library's own copies under vendor/golang.org/x/. golang.org/x/crypto is listed in the Go build information of both programs (v0.47.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r3, v0.49.0 in 0.31.1-r4, v0.50.0 in 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r1, v0.52.0 in 0.32.1-r2 to 0.32.2-r0, then v0.53.0 rising to v0.58.0 by 0.34.1-r2), but the only golang.org/x/crypto packages compiled into any build are bcrypt and blowfish in alertmanager and bcrypt in amtool. No build contains any function from golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, so none of the advisory's vulnerable symbols (Dial, NewClientConn, NewServerConn, the Client and Server methods of the curve25519sha256, dhGEXSHA, dhGroup, ecdh and mlkem768WithCurve25519sha256 key exchanges, gcmCipher.readCipherPacket) is present. Positive control: the same search finds runtime.main and golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt functions in every binary, and finds golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.NewServerConn, ssh.Dial in a stripped test program built for linux/amd64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.50.0. The vulnerable code is not compiled into any build of this package.

Each package holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/build. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index, every entry with the same source commit and installed size as 2.19.1-r0; the copy the repository serves was read. /usr/bin/build links functions the advisory lists in every build, among them golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.Dial, NewClientConn and the AES-GCM decoder (*gcmCipher).readCipherPacket. statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-46597 (GO-2026-5013, GHSA-q4h4-gmj2-qvw2): an incorrectly placed cast from bytes to int in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh AES-GCM packet decoder let well-crafted input cause an underflow and a server-side panic. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 by commit abbc44d, which changes ssh/cipher.go: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5013, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q4h4-gmj2-qvw2, https://go.dev/issue/79561, https://go.dev/cl/781620, https://github.com/golang/crypto/commit/abbc44d451a6f9236a2bbd26cbcd4d0fec473da3. The Go vulnerability database lists these golang.org/x/crypto/ssh functions as vulnerable: Dial, NewClientConn, NewServerConn, gcmCipher.readCipherPacket, and the Client and Server methods of the curve25519sha256, dhGEXSHA, dhGroup, ecdh and mlkem768WithCurve25519sha256 key exchanges. We read every published external-dns-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64: 33 versions, 0.20.0-r0 to 0.24.0-r5, each matching its repository index checksum. We also read every published external-dns package in that repository and every external-dns-fips and external-dns-fips-dev package in the authenticated DHI Alpine security repository (33 versions each, 0.20.0-r0 to 0.24.0-r5, both architectures), 264 packages in all. Each of these packages holds exactly one file, /usr/bin/external-dns, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Its Go build information lists the golang.org/x/crypto module (v0.45.0 to v0.58.0 across these builds), but none of them links golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: a Go function-table (pclntab) reader finds no function under golang.org/x/crypto/ssh in any of the 264 programs, other than the init function of the separate golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/terminal package in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r13, a wrapper around golang.org/x/term that does not contain the affected code. statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-46597 (GO-2026-5013): An incorrectly placed cast from bytes to int allowed for server-side panic in the AES-GCM packet decoder for well-crafted inputs. The flaw is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package and is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5013, https://go.dev/issue/79561, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI, https://go.dev/cl/781620). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain. The Go source tree it ships vendors a few golang.org/x/crypto packages for the standard library under /usr/lib/go/src/vendor, and its cmd tree vendors no golang.org/x/crypto package. In no published build is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh among them. Checked every published golang-1.26-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (1.26.4-0 to 1.26.11-18, amd64 and arm64), together with the oci-config and debug-symbol (dbgsym) packages built from the same source: none contains a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh directory or source file, and no ELF file in them (including the go and gofmt commands and the tools under /usr/lib/go/pkg/tool) contains golang.org/x/crypto/ssh code or symbols. The golang-1.26-dev-fips-oci-config packages built from the same source in the DHI Debian security repository for Debian 13 hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog, and no program. A Go program that uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh takes it from its own golang.org/x/crypto requirement, not from the toolchain, so it is fixed by upgrading golang.org/x/crypto in that program.
